NDT Level III consulting in Oklahoma City: depot and MRO aviation, oilfield equipment and pipeline programs, and the local options

Oklahoma City's NDT activity splits between aviation sustainment and energy. Tinker Air Force Base hosts the Oklahoma City Air Logistics Complex and the Air Force Nondestructive Inspection Office, commercial heavy maintenance runs at Will Rogers World Airport, and the FAA's Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center sits on the southwest side. On the energy side, oilfield equipment makers, repair shops and pipeline contractors need written practices and procedures their customers will accept. Atlantis provides NDT consulting to both groups as ASNT NDT Level III work, done remotely from Houston with trips to Oklahoma sites for examinations and audits.

What do Oklahoma City companies ask an NDT Level III for?

  • Aviation repair stations and component shops: written practices, procedures and examinations that fit a Part 145 repair station manual and the OEM's NDT instructions. AAR's Oklahoma City airframe facility, for example, lists magnetic particle, fluorescent penetrant, eddy current and ultrasonic capability to ASTM E1444, ASTM E1417 and OEM requirements, the kind of scope a supplier's program has to mirror.
  • Depot subcontractors whose people work alongside Air Force NDI staff and must show their own qualification records.
  • Oilfield equipment manufacturers and service shops: MT and UT procedures for pressure-containing and load-bearing parts built to API product specifications and customer drawings.
  • Pipeline and midstream contractors: weld inspection procedures and personnel records that satisfy the operator's specification. For plant work, see refining NDT consulting in Oklahoma City.

Rules that apply in Oklahoma

Boilers and pressure vessels in Oklahoma are regulated through the Oklahoma Department of Labor's Safety Standards Division. Oklahoma is an NRC Agreement State, so radiography contractors on Oklahoma sites hold state licenses, and Atlantis does not perform radiography in the US. Air Force NDI personnel follow the Air Force program set out under Air Force Instruction 21-105, while FAA repair stations follow 14 CFR Part 145, so a contractor serving both should keep the two sets of requirements clearly separated in its documents.

Non-destructive testing schools in Oklahoma, and the consulting options

People looking for NDT schools in Oklahoma will find Spartan College of Aeronautics and Technology, whose Tulsa NDT and quality-control program splits time between hands-on work and theory, and OSU Institute of Technology, whose pipeline integrity associate degree includes NDT. Schools train technicians; they do not certify them, because under SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies. For Level III support the choices are an in-house Level III; the Level III of an inspection company, such as IRISNDT, which lists Tulsa and Ponca City locations, or Mistras, Acuren and ATS, which describe Level III services nationally; or a remote outsourced Level III.

How to vet an NDT Level III consultant in Oklahoma City

  • Aviation: ask how the consultant handles an OEM manual that calls for a technique your written practice does not yet cover.
  • Oilfield: ask for a procedure written to an API product specification, and check the acceptance criteria come from that specification rather than habit.
  • Read the method list on the ASNT certificate. If your shop runs eddy current, find out who will be the ET Level III.
  • Ask how practical examination specimens are sourced and documented, since depot and OEM auditors look at them closely, and whether the specimens contain real or simulated discontinuities.
  • Where the consultant's company also performs inspection, decide who checks its reports before you sign.

How Atlantis supports Oklahoma City companies

Each engagement is run by Anoop Rayavarapu, an ASNT NDT Level III certificate holder for UT, RT, MT, PT and VT; for those methods, Atlantis can take the outside agency Level III role. Documents are written and reviewed remotely, and practical examinations and audits are held at your shop or hangar. For hands-on training, technicians study theory online at their own pace, practise in the Practical NDT simulator, then complete the practical at the employer's facility under its written practice; see NDT training in Oklahoma City.
